questions.title: Bernoulli probability as the unique minimizer of expected Brier loss
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Brier (1950) and Gneiting and Raftery (2007). Let Y be Bernoulli(q), let a probability forecast p lie in [0,1], and define the Brier loss L(p,Y)=(p-Y)^2. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX Theory workspace, derive the population risk exactly, prove the decomposition R_q(p)=q(1-q)+(p-q)^2, and conclude that q is the unique population minimizer with excess risk (p-q)^2, including q=0 and q=1. Derive the finite-sample empirical-risk decomposition for binary observations and prove that the sample event rate is the unique empirical minimizer over [0,1], including all-zero and all-one samples. Distinguish this unconditional Bernoulli result from calibration or optimality claims for heterogeneous covariate-dependent forecasts, and do not use simulation or a library call as proof. The required model-authored Python artifact is est_brier_bernoulli_mean and must implement run_estimator(request) exactly for the frozen public closed contract, returning the empirical event rate, mean Brier loss at the supplied forecast, minimum empirical Brier loss, and empirical excess loss. Exploratory Python or R may check the algebra, edge cases, invariances, and finite-sample behavior. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment invokes the estimator under multiple predeclared Bernoulli probabilities, compares event-rate error at increasing sample sizes, and compares out-of-sample Brier loss with predeclared off-target forecasts using Monte Carlo uncertainty. That assessment is implementation and finite-sample evidence, not proof of strict propriety or a general calibration theorem. Source-code replication, conditional probability estimation, interval estimation, novelty, and Lean formalization are not applicable.

primary_paper.title: Verification of Forecasts Expressed in Terms of Probability

public_mathematical_context.title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
public_mathematical_context.journal: Journal of the American Statistical Association

request_fields.name: outcomes
request_fields.meaning: Observed binary outcomes used to form the empirical event rate and empirical Brier risk.
request_fields.shape: one array of length 1 through 5000 containing exact JSON integers 0 or 1
request_fields.indexing: sample order is arbitrary and must not affect the response
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, floats including 0.0 and 1.0, strings, other integers, empty arrays, oversized arrays, and nested arrays rather than coercing or dropping them.

request_fields.name: forecast
request_fields.meaning: Probability forecast at which empirical Brier loss is evaluated.
request_fields.shape: one finite JSON number in the closed interval [0,1]
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, strings, nonnumeric or nonfinite values, and values outside [0,1] rather than clipping or coercing them.

response_fields.name: event_rate
response_fields.meaning: Empirical mean of the binary outcomes.
response_fields.edge_cases: Return exactly 0 for an all-zero sample and exactly 1 for an all-one sample.

response_fields.name: mean_brier_loss
response_fields.edge_cases: Use every observation exactly once and the supplied forecast without clipping or replacement.

response_fields.name: optimal_mean_brier_loss
response_fields.meaning: Minimum empirical mean Brier loss attained at the empirical event rate.
response_fields.edge_cases: It is zero for all-zero and all-one samples.

response_fields.name: excess_brier_loss
response_fields.meaning: Empirical Brier loss above its sample minimum.

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly outcomes and forecast and the response contains exactly event_rate, mean_brier_loss, optimal_mean_brier_loss, and excess_brier_loss. Missing or extra fields and invalid values are rejected rather than ignored, repaired, clipped, or coerced.
For every valid request, mean_brier_loss equals optimal_mean_brier_loss plus excess_brier_loss, where the latter equals (forecast-event_rate)^2.
Permuting request.outcomes leaves every response field unchanged.
Replacing every outcome y by 1-y and forecast by 1-forecast replaces event_rate by 1-event_rate while leaving all three Brier-loss fields unchanged.

empirical_claims.meaning: Before outcomes, freeze each Bernoulli probability, sample size, seed, replicate count, off-target comparator, estimator invocation, out-of-sample evaluation rule, and Monte Carlo decision rule.

For multiple predeclared Bernoulli probabilities, compare empirical event-rate error at increasing sample sizes and compare out-of-sample Brier loss with predeclared off-target forecasts using Monte Carlo standard errors.

The confirmatory assessment checks the executable decomposition and finite-sample behavior only. It does not prove strict propriety, establish a conditional calibration theorem, fit a conditional probability model, provide intervals, reproduce source code, establish novelty, or provide formal proof evidence.
